Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from Saudi Arabia’s coastal Ras Tanura peninsula after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed to have attacked the kingdom’s biggest oil refinery.
Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the strikes “were accurate and direct” and caused a fire to break out at the Ras Tanura facility, which is part of one of the world’s largest crude oil export terminals.
A shipping source told CNN Thursday that oil loadings at the terminal were suspended in the aftermath of the attack. It’s unclear whether they have resumed.
The Houthis have targeted infrastructure in Saudi Arabia repeatedly in recent weeks – including an attack on the capital Riyadh’s financial district – as the fallout from the US-Iran war drags on. Riyadh’s international airport was also hit several times last month, killing more than a dozen people.

Young Britons are having half as much sex as they were in 1990, according to a new study, with the average reported frequency falling from four times a month to just twice a month.
The data was produced as part of a long-running study known as the National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), according to a statement Wednesday from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM), which participates in the research.
